newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian votes in socialists, awaits government.
newsitem.headline: Albanian votes in socialists, awaits government.

text.p: Albanians put the opposition Socialists in office and awaited the formation of a leftist coalition government after five years of growing authoritarian rule by President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party.

Sunday's run-off elections in 34 of 115 electoral districts will have little effect on the overall outcome of the country's fourth post-communist election -- intended to consolidate order and end months of turmoil in which 1,500 people have died.
Socialists captured more than 80 of the legislature's 155 seats in last week's first round and party leader Fatos Nano has already said he will be the next prime Minster.

He also predicted the Socialists and two allied parties would win the two-thirds majority needed to push legislation through unhindered and remove Berisha if he reverses his campaign commitment to leave office if the left won power.
"The coalition government has got two thirds. There is no doubt about that," Nano said at his polling station on Sunday.
"It is very sure now, with this already large mandate, that people voted in this election for a new way of rebuilding a democratic civilisation in Albania."
Nano repeatedly stressed during a hard-fought campaign that his party had shed the legacy of its predecessor, the hard-line Communist Party which ruled Albania for 45 years.
Praised initially by the West for steering Albania onto the path of market economics, Berisha fell foul of public opinion over the collapse of four pyramid investment schemes this year.

The fall of the schemes -- with the savings of countless thousands in Europe's poorest country -- triggered rioting and looting of arms depots stemmed only when Berisha appointed a multi-party government and called the early election.
A 7,000-strong international protection force has maintained a precarious peace but Italy, its main backer, has said the troops will be pulled out some time in August.
The first round of voting took nearly a week to tally, but electoral officials suggested results would be forthcoming more quickly this time with only two finalists in each district.

Hours after the polls closed, a single result was announced by the official ATA news agency -- Neritan Ceka of the Democratic Alliance, allied to the Socialists, defeated another leftist candidate in the central city of Elbasan.
If all goes according to plan, once the new parliament is convened it will elect a new president who can then formally agree to Nano's appointment as prime minister.
His choice to take the premier's job was an indication that he wished to reduce what many see as the inordinate amount of powers taken on by Berisha during his five years in office.

Nano wants the head of the interim government, fellow Socialist Bashkim Fino, alongside him in his new administration. Newspapers have speculated the new president could be Socialist Party Secretary General Rexhep Mejdani.
Officials said up to three constituencies in Sunday's voting could go through to yet another round of voting next Sunday because of legal and procedural challenges.
The latest races were closely watched for the second week running by monitors under the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe.
Its top official, Catherine Lalumiere, said she saw no irregularities serious enough to jeopardise the poll despite complaints registered by both major parties.

Other races being closely watched included two seats in Tirana -- Former Democratic prime minister Aleksander Meksi, and a top Berisha adviser Fatos Beja -- who were trying to buck the trend and win seats in the run-off.
In Kavaje, once an unassailable Democratic Party stronghold southwest of Tirana, three Democratic standardbearers were also locked in second round battles.
